cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven strip cloth (Njaye kpoikpoi) with indigo supplementary-weft designs forming a central cross and box motif, a documented Sherbro textile type made and used ceremonially by this Sierra Leone people.

physical.title: cloth; textile
physical.summary: Display cloth (Njaye kpoikpoi), composed of 11 strips of hand-spun cotton of white and indigo, which are hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. Each strip has a different design that are designed so that they create a single design across the entire cloth, which is otherwise white. The design consists of two wide bands of supplementary weft floats in indigo that run across each end of the cloth.These flank rectangles (of which each strip has two) that are aligned to form a large cross that dominates the cloth, and which touch at the centre the corners of a large central box (called a tenoi in Mende) that itself frames a smaller rectangle that encloses two diamond motifs. At random points across the cloth small floating motifs, including diamond, chevron and striped squares, have been added in pink and indigo cotton in discontinuous supplementary weft. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
